rv.q: Troubles and screams both sing out in The Surge, an ode to her by American choreographer Sonya Tayeh. The singer, who died in 2023, attracted both worship and scorn in her lifetime. The Surge is an act of devotion – 10 women sit on pews, swaying, sliding and indeed surging around them.

Dance, by its nature, tends to be ageist. The wear and tear which the dance discipline makes upon bodies nudges dancers towards very early retirement or less demanding ‘character’ roles. The ten woman dancers involved in The Surge are, however, older than the norm demonstrating age is not something to fear or avoid.
Joyce Theater’s dull dance tribute to Sinéad O’Connor misses the singer’s transcendence

It is a simple idea, but one that gives the production an added sense of honesty and warmth. From the moment the audience enters The Hall at Aviva Studios, it is clear this is not a conventional dance production. Tom Visser’s set design makes excellent use of the vast space, creating a setting that feels intimate despite its scale.
